finding_verification.evidence: In _publish_no_replace (src/argus/runtime/data_root_marker_store.py), the outer try/finally protecting the acquired HANDLE now begins immediately after the CreateFileW success check, with no unprotected code between HANDLE acquisition and the start of protection. UTF-16 target-path conversion, FILE_RENAME_INFO buffer construction, and the SetFileInformationByHandle call are all inside this protected region, and CloseHandle in the finally block runs on every exit path. An inner try/except narrowly catches (UnicodeEncodeError, MemoryError, OverflowError) -- the specific runtime failure types possible in that construction code -- and converts them to a plain OSError, which the caller's existing except OSError handling maps to MarkerAtomicWriteFailed. No broad except Exception catch-all was introduced; a programming-error exception type outside that tuple would remain uncaught, consistent with the clarified Contract's explicit programming-error boundary (Contract #7.2, paragraphs added in the 2026-09-18 and subsequent clarification).

finding_verification.evidence: tests/component/test_data_root_marker_store_contract_v03.py adds exactly one new test, test_finding_02_valid_but_different_reload_keeps_published_target, confirmed by direct diff against v02.py to be a pure addition with zero changes to any existing test. The new test monkeypatches only load_data_root_marker to return a valid LoadedDataRootMarker whose marker differs from the intended marker in data_root_id, exercises the real publish path, and asserts MarkerReloadVerificationFailed, that the published target file still exists, and that its bytes equal the intended marker's serialization (i.e. no automatic repair toward the reloaded content). This closes the previously-unexercised branch of Contract #7.4's reload domain-equality requirement.
